title: White Mulberry: Ancient Silk Mulberries You Can Visit
meta_description: Planted as machinery: white mulberry leaf is all a silkworm will eat. The Green Lady of Krka, about 400 years old, outlived Dalmatia's silk trade.
intro: These trees were planted as machinery. White mulberry leaf is the only thing a silkworm will eat, so every ruler who fancied a silk industry ordered mulberries into the ground, and the trees stayed long after the venture folded. At the Krka falls in Croatia, the Green Lady stands below the ruins of a mill, about 400 years old by the national park's account; in the 1830s nearby Skradin was the largest silkworm-breeding centre in Dalmatia. Maria Theresa's push put orchards across Taban in Buda, which is most likely where Budapest's oldest mulberry comes from, whatever the Ottoman legend says. Around Bergamo the leaves fed trays of larvae in farmhouse lofts, and three of those trees still stand in a public garden. Split's, in the courtyard of Hajduk's first ground, was DNA sampled in 2015 and cloned 105 times, once per year of the club.
